title: Look before you act
concept: Run a block only when a condition about the world is True, with else for the other case

steps.say: Run it: move, then pick, 6 times.
Look first: `if gems_here():` picks only where there is a gem.
After the run, which gems are still on the row?
Gems in other places, same code. Run it.
`front_is_clear()` asks about the cell ahead. `else:` runs when the `if` is False. Run it.
Walk the row: a `for` loop that runs `move()` 8 times.
After `move()`, look: add `if gems_here():` inside the loop.
Indent `pick()` under the `if`, so it runs only on a gem.
Run it. Your program is also tried in other worlds, with gems in other places.

guided.done: Every gem picked, wherever it was.

recap.say: `if condition:` runs its block only when the condition is True; `else:` runs when it is False. `not` flips True and False.

fill_gaps: Compare your result with the Goal view: each cell ends with exactly one gem.
`put()` on a full cell makes two. You need the opposite question: is this cell empty? The word `not` turns True into False.
flip_row: Watch a world that failed, one cell at a time. What happens on a cell that had a gem? On one that didn't?
Two separate `if`s: after the first picks a gem, what does the second one see? Which keyword makes only one block run?
detour: Replay a world that failed and watch where the robot stops: at the wall, or short of the end?
Each pass: step, or go around. How far along the top lane must the robot go? So how many passes does the walk need?
